output.summary: Deterministic verdict: capacity is BOUNDED on load axis "users" (unit count) with lower_inclusive 197 and upper_exclusive 297, policy_verdict PASS. Run validity is VALID and analysis coverage is COMPLETE. Stage-1 (target 100, achieved 97) and stage-2 (target 200, achieved 197) passed their latency policy and generator diagnostic guard, defining the verified bound. Stage-3 (target 300, achieved 297) failed the overall latency policy (response_time_p95_ms observed 420 > threshold 250), so it is excluded from the bound and sets upper_exclusive 297. capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, a fixed product limitation, not a defect of the run. The generator-cpu diagnostic guard (effect: diagnostic, threshold 0.85) passed in all three stages with generator CPU around 0.43. All window summaries report resource_verdict NO_POLICY, which is distinct from PASS and FAIL. The advice below does not change the deterministic verdict.

hypotheses.observation: policy-check-window for stage-3 reports response_time_p95_ms observed 420, operator lte, threshold 250, status FAIL; window-policy-summary for stage-3 reports verdict FAIL (business_verdict FAIL); capacity_summary lists stage-3 verdict FAIL with verified_bound_load 297.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The stage-3 latency breach (p95 420 ms > 250 ms) is the reason that stage is excluded from the capacity bound; the system under test may have degraded or queued at approximately 300 users, but no server-side metrics are present to confirm the cause.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the per-10s p95 latency series for the stage-3 window (from_epoch_ms 1767226200000 to_epoch_ms 1767226500000) to see when the breach begins and whether it is sustained; collect any available server-side telemetry for the same window.

hypotheses.observation: generator-cpu resource summaries show mean ~0.43 with slope 0 in each stage; the resource-policy-check generator-cpu-guard (effect: diagnostic, operator gt, threshold 0.85) has status PASS in stage-1, stage-2, and stage-3.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Generator-side resource exhaustion is not supported by the available evidence: if generator overload caused the stage-3 latency breach, the diagnostic guard would be expected to fail, but it passed at ~0.43 CPU, far below 0.85.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Review the active_users and generator-cpu series for stage-3 for anomalies beyond the summary statistics, and rerun with a healthy generator while keeping the guard effect diagnostic (do not change its effect to binding, SLA, or enforcing).

hypotheses.observation: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, with explicit evaluation and snapshot windows aligned to run epoch values but clock alignment not verified.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment, no lead/lag or temporal ordering between applied load and observed latency can be established; clock skew could misplace observations across stages.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment among load generator, system under test, and timing sources before drawing any temporal or causal conclusions.

hypotheses.observation: metric-summary-overall reports error_count 0, latency_ms p95 417, p99 420, max 1500; the stage-3 policy check reports p95 observed 420 with status FAIL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run shows no errors at the overall summary level despite the stage-3 p95 latency breach; the latency increase without observed errors could indicate queueing or contention rather than request failures, but summary-level data do not prove this.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Examine per-window and per-bin error, latency, and throughput series to determine whether any stage-3 samples approached the 1500 ms max and whether errors appear at finer granularity.

recommendations.action: Treat certified capacity as BOUNDED with lower_inclusive 197 and upper_exclusive 297 users; if capability at 300 users with p95 <= 250 ms is required, address the stage-3 latency breach before rerunning.
recommendations.rationale: Stage-1 and stage-2 passed their latency policy and define the verified bound; stage-3 failed its latency policy (420 > 250) and is excluded, producing upper_exclusive 297.

recommendations.action: Rerun stage-3 after confirming load-generator health from the active_users and generator-cpu series; inspect the generator's resource series and keep the generator-cpu-guard effect diagnostic.
recommendations.rationale: The generator diagnostic guard (effect: diagnostic, threshold 0.85) passed in all stages with CPU ~0.43, so the stage-3 failure is not attributable to generator saturation on the available evidence; a clean rerun with a healthy generator helps isolate the latency breach.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment before correlating applied load with latency observations across windows.
recommendations.rationale: clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so temporal ordering between load and observed latency is not established; clock verification is a prerequisite for lead/lag reasoning.

recommendations.action: Confirm the intended policy configuration for the latency rule (rule_id 'latency', overall scope, threshold 250 ms) and keep NO_POLICY resource verdicts distinct from pass and fail when interpreting windows.
recommendations.rationale: All three window summaries report resource_verdict NO_POLICY (no resource SLA rule applied in the window); only the business latency policy is evaluated (observed 140, 140, 420 vs threshold 250). NO_POLICY is not a pass and not a failure.

caveats: capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; this is a fixed product limitation, not a defect of this run, and there is no knee-detector step the operator can take.
resource_verdict NO_POLICY appears in every window-policy-summary; missing applicable resource SLA rules mean those values are neither PASS nor FAIL, and NO_POLICY stays NO_POLICY.

The capacity bound is derived only from stages with a verified product outcome (stage-1 and stage-2 passed; stage-3 failed and is excluded). Achieved loads 97, 197, 297 are p05_10s statistics, and the epoch values in resource-binding are timestamps, not durations.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypothesis is supported by this dataset.

Overall run metrics (error_count 0, sample_count 3601, latency p95 417/p99 420) are whole-run summaries; they are a different scope from the per-stage policy checks and do not prove absence of degradation within any specific stage.

No server-side (system under test) resource metrics are present in the evidence; only load-generator metrics and transaction/overall latency summaries are available, so the cause of the stage-3 latency breach cannot be confirmed from this dataset.

The generator-cpu-guard is diagnostic by contract; its PASS status supports generator health but does not by itself certify SUT capacity, and its effect must not be changed to binding, SLA, or enforcing.
